solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Many think 5/21 should have, giving up the ghost, maybe

definitions.note: the answer completes the sentence as a past participle phrase
definitions.meaning: first meaning: been sacked, as many wanted after the presenter's scandal

definitions.note: a jokey picture of dying; the answer is past tense where the definition is a participle
definitions.meaning: second meaning, flagged by maybe: shoved off this mortal coil

explanation.walkthrough: 5/21 is Jonathan Ross, suspended by the BBC in 2008 over prank calls; many wanted him fired outright. 'Maybe' marks the second sense, dying, as a playful stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the push is a British idiom for being dismissed from a job, and loosely for being pushed out of life.

clue.text: (& 18dn.) Arses were concerned in having kittens

definitions.note: a participial phrase standing for an adjective describing a state of terror

parts.note: a coarse plural word for contemptible people
to care is to be concerned, here in the past tense

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant people were worried about a cat giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for the arses runs straight on into the word for being concerned; the split falls after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Having kittens is a British idiom for being in a state of extreme anxiety or fright, which the coarse compound describes.

clue.text: Brown turned up after work as one dreading the next election?

indicators.note: placed after means the first element follows the second in the answer
in a down clue, turning something up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: Gordon Brown was Prime Minister, abbreviated PM, when this was set

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown appeared at work, fearing the coming vote.
explanation.walkthrough: PM reversed becomes MP. Brown led a deeply unpopular Labour government heading for the 2010 election.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labour member of Parliament in 2008 faced likely defeat, so would be dreading the polls; the question mark marks this as a description.

clue.text: Sod off, grabbing dog's front bits

indicators.note: something off is out of order, so the letters must be shuffled
grabbing means holding something within its grip, so one piece goes inside another
the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal aimed at someone pinching bits of a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds, as in odds and ends, are miscellaneous small items or scraps.

clue.text: (& 21ac.) Swift, perhaps, to associate with rubbish, no depth, an unwelcome caller

parts.note: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels; perhaps marks him as one of many with the first name

indicators.note: no depth means the abbreviation for depth is taken away

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A satirical swipe linking a quick person with rubbish and a nuisance caller.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2008 Ross and Russell Brand left lewd voicemails on actor Andrew Sachs's phone during a BBC radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: The presenter phoned Andrew Sachs and left offensive messages, making him a caller nobody welcomed.

clue.text: Obama's mixed blood group changed — responsible for fall-out

indicators.note: mixed letters are jumbled into a new order
a blood group being changed means one group letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: the blood groups A and B are single letters; one A becomes B

explanation.surface: A comment on Obama's mixed heritage being blamed for a political row.
explanation.walkthrough: After the shuffle, the final A (blood group A) is replaced by B (blood group B).
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic bomb produces radioactive fallout, so it is the thing responsible for it.

clue.text: Screwed only with the ends of nacreous hose

indicators.note: screwed up means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of pearly stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose means stockings, and nylons are stockings made of nylon.

clue.text: see 15ac.
15/8 and 5/21's 25 did — Obama doesn't have a right to get excited

indicators.note: not having something means that element is removed

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A political jibe about an excitable Obama, tied to the presenters' scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 15/8 is Russell Brand, 5/21 Jonathan Ross, 25 PRANK: their phone stunt on Andrew Sachs rebounded on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that backfires has the opposite effect to that intended, as the prank calls did, costing Brand his job.

clue.text: Went to a cafe and performed a sex act?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dined away from home
second meaning: vulgar slang for oral sex

explanation.walkthrough: The innocent meal and the vulgar slang share one phrase; the question mark flags the rude second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating out means having a meal at a restaurant, and is also crude slang for performing oral sex.

clue.text: City pissed off with last of lucre, sport!

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A town angry about money, followed by an exclamation of 'sport!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed off' looks like an anagram indicator but is a single word for angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks, so it is a sport.

clue.text: Either way, not a body 5/21 will be performing on for a while

definitions.text: not a body 5/21 will be performing on for a while

parts.note: surface reading: whichever way you look at it, some organisation

parts.words: 5/21 will be performing on for a while
parts.note: setter's reading: the broadcaster that suspended the presenter, whose nickname reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, the presenter will be off some network for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either way' hints that the answer reads the same forwards and backwards. The Beeb is the British nickname for the BBC, which suspended Jonathan Ross for twelve weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC suspended its presenter without pay after the prank calls, so he would not appear on its channels for a time.

clue.text: Fickle fashion so abandoned Kureishi?

indicators.note: something fickle keeps changing, so the remaining letters change order
letters that are abandoned are left out of the word

explanation.surface: A writer dropped because fashion is fickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanif Kureishi is the British novelist of The Buddha of Suburbia; the question mark signals the first name is defined by surname.

clue.text: Not quite pissed when there's an equal amount left in the glass

definitions.text: when there's an equal amount left in the glass
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a glass emptied to its midpoint

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk. One sense is a tipsy person, the other a glass whose contents are half consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-drunk describes a person partly intoxicated and also a drink of which half has been consumed.

clue.text: Right providing the ultimate in socialist schism

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: the ultimate letter in a word is its last one

explanation.surface: A political split between right and left.
explanation.walkthrough: The political right and socialists in the surface lead toward party politics; they are only sources of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a split or division between groups, which is what a schism is.

clue.text: Mug putting money in the bank — prime concern of politician who's ballsed up?

definitions.text: prime concern of politician who's ballsed up?

explanation.surface: A fool banking cash, and a politician who has made a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' reads as a gullible person, but here it is slang for the face. 'Ballsed up' is British slang for bungled.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who has blundered is chiefly anxious to avoid humiliation and preserve reputation, which is face-saving.

clue.text: (& 8ac.) Take stock on the radio and mark? This broadcaster didn't

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is received by ear, so spelling follows sound

parts.note: to rustle is to steal livestock
a brand is an identifying mark
surface padding: a jibe that he failed to stop and think before his radio prank

explanation.surface: A broadcaster who failed to pause and consider before acting on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take stock' wants to mean reflect; it is stealing cattle. The tail jokes that Brand didn't take stock, thinking before his notorious 2008 radio prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Russell Brand presented a BBC Radio 2 show, so he was a broadcaster.

clue.text: A N Wilson's screwed up as a person, relatively speaking

indicators.note: screwed up means twisted and crumpled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the writer's name, without the possessive S

explanation.surface: The writer A N Wilson has made a mess as a person.
explanation.walkthrough: A N Wilson is a British journalist and biographer; the 's is read as 'is', not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A son-in-law is a person related by marriage, so he is a person speaking in terms of relations.

clue.text: Jerks off PRO inside steamy location?

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
placed inside means set within another word

parts.note: tics are involuntary jerks of the muscles

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of a prostitute in a steamy room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks off' wants to be a single crude phrase; split it, and 'Jerks' is the outer word while 'off' scrambles the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the hot, humid regions near the equator, a steamy place.

clue.text: see 2dn.
A foreigner to Prince Philip lacks tail feature

indicators.note: lacking a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: an offensive slur for a Chinese person, the kind of term the gaffe-prone Duke of Edinburgh was mocked for

explanation.surface: Mockery of Prince Philip's famous gaffes about foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye satire: the Duke, the Queen's husband, was notorious for racially insensitive remarks, including one about 'slitty eyes' in China.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is a part of the face, and facial parts are called features.

clue.text: Cameron's opening on entering went badly with audience — cut up

indicators.note: entering means going inside another word

parts.note: a performer who dies on stage fails to win the crowd

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: David Cameron flopped with his audience as soon as he walked in.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice is to cut food into small cubes, so diced means cut up.

clue.text: see 5ac.
Twelve-inch woody, perhaps, for Brenda?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wooden measuring stick a foot long
second meaning: what the Queen is, Brenda being Private Eye's name for her

explanation.walkthrough: 'Woody' plays on a crude slang sense; it means made of wood. Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a straight measuring strip, often wooden and a foot long, and also a sovereign such as the Queen.

clue.text: At heart, Blair gets due — near distraught as a leader no more

indicators.note: distraught means deeply upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, close to getting his deserts, is distraught at no longer leading.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair suggests a British leader, but the answer is a German one.
explanation.definitionFit: Konrad Adenauer was West Germany's first chancellor after the war; he died in 1967, so he leads no longer.

clue.text: Have a bash at exercise, weed!

parts.note: a do or bash is a party, so to have a bash is to have a do

explanation.surface: A call to throw a party at the gym, along with some cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope and weed are both slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Lisa, broadcasting on Five has a gob

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters material widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A presenter called Lisa, broadcasting on the TV channel Five, has a big mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gob' reads as mouth; here it is the British slang noun for spit. Five is a UK television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gob is British slang for a lump of spittle, and spit is saliva.

clue.text: Straw makes it easier to separate Brenda from fool

indicators.note: separating one thing from another removes it from the whole

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible fool
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, who is ER

explanation.surface: Using a straw helps to keep the Queen apart from a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher. Jack Straw, then Justice Secretary, hides behind the drinking straw.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking straw lets one draw liquid up through it, so it makes the action of sucking easier.

clue.text: Pressure managed to get to Barack finally — just a joke?

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pressure finally gets to Obama: was it all a joke?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at the Sachs calls, defended as just a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank is a practical joke or trick played on someone.

clue.text: Principle of gettin' castrated if articulated?

indicators.note: articulated means spoken, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: to doctor an animal is to neuter it; the dropped g mirrors the clue's own

explanation.surface: A sly question about the principle behind neutering, spoken in a casual accent.
explanation.walkthrough: To doctor a pet is a euphemism for castrating it. Said with a dropped g, doctorin' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a principle or body of beliefs taught and held by a group.
